title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is an abelian variety of dimension n, A' another abelian variety, and u : A → A' a homomorphism. Write u_1 : T_ℓ(A) → T_ℓ(A') for the map on Tate modules, which is the map on H_1, tensored with Q_ℓ. Grothendieck computes the pushforward u_*(1_A) of the fundamental class of A.

For an abelian variety, ℓ-adic homology is the exterior algebra on H_1 = V_ℓ(A) = T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ. So the top-degree class lives in Λ^{2n} V_ℓ(A), twisted by (-n) so that it becomes a Tate-twist-free line ≅ Q_ℓ. This is what he writes as H^{2n}(A) = (Λ^{2n} T_{Q_ℓ}(A))(-n). Read via Poincaré duality on A', the pushforward is u_*(1_A) = (Λ^{2n} u_1 ⊗ Q_ℓ(-n))(fundamental class) ∈ Λ^{2n} V_ℓ(A')(-n).

Consequence: when u_1 is injective (u has finite kernel, i.e. is an isogeny onto its image), Λ^{2n}u_1 applied to a generator is a nonzero decomposable 2n-vector. Its Plücker point determines the 2n-dimensional subspace u_1(V_ℓ(A)) ⊂ V_ℓ(A'). So the cycle class of the abelian subvariety u(A) (up to the degree factor) determines the image of the Tate module.

Context: this belongs to the cote-14 notes on algebraic cycles and the Tate, Hodge and Lefschetz conjectures. Presumably it relates cycle classes of abelian subvarieties to ℓ-adic subrepresentations, as in the abelian-variety case of the Tate conjecture. The neighbouring pages are from an unrelated typed text on Čech cohomology of ringed sites and acyclicity criteria; they are a different document misfiled in the same cote.
errors: Over Z_ℓ the claim is only true up to saturation. The decomposable vector Λ^{2n}u_1(generator) in Λ^{2n}T_ℓ(A') determines the Q_ℓ-subspace u_1(V_ℓ(A)), and its divisibility gives the index of the lattice. It does not determine the lattice u_1(T_ℓ(A)) itself. The statement should be read rationally (V_ℓ), consistent with Grothendieck's T_{Q_ℓ} notation.

Notational looseness: the group written H^{2n}(A) = Λ^{2n}T(A)(-n) is really top homology (or H^{2n} after Poincaré duality / dualization). u_*(1_A) naturally lies in H^{2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n), which is Poincaré dual to Λ^{2n}V_ℓ(A'). The formula is correct up to this identification and the twist conventions.

ideas.what: Pushforward of the fundamental class of an abelian variety under a homomorphism equals the top exterior power of the induced map on H_1 = Tate module.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of abelian varieties as an exterior algebra; functoriality of cycle class / Gysin map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Weil, Lang, Mumford's Abelian Varieties; Milne)

ideas.what: The cycle class of an abelian subvariety determines its rational Tate module, via the Plücker embedding of the Grassmannian.
ideas.modern_name: Plücker coordinates of the subspace V_ℓ(B) ⊂ V_ℓ(A'); relation between abelian subvarieties and Galois-stable subspaces in the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; cf. Tate (1966), Faltings (1983) for the Galois-module side

deep.surprise_reason: A short routine linear-algebra remark: the pushforward of the fundamental class is Λ^{2n} of the Tate-module map, and it determines the image subspace by Plücker. It is standard and has no new content, though it shows Grothendieck relating cycle classes of abelian subvarieties to Tate modules around 1965–71.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the struck-out fragment reads roughly '[-à partir-] u_*(1_A) ∈ Λ^{2n} T_{Q_ℓ}(A')(-n)', which is a correction of the target group. The transcription's rendering is acceptable.
Line 4: the map is written 'Λ^{2n} u_1 ⊗ Q_ℓ(-n)', with u_1 (subscript 1, the H_1 map) rather than u_s.
Line 6: 'au [-premier-]...' is likely 'du premier membre' (the struck-out word under 'premier' looks like 'membre'), i.e. 'the fundamental class of the first member'.
Last line: plausibly 'dans le cas où u_1 est bien injectif' (or 'où celui-ci est injectif'); the injectivity condition refers to u_1 on Tate modules, i.e. u with finite kernel.
Page 84 contains only this manuscript fragment. The 'previous' and 'next' typed pages (Prop. 3.1, Déf. 3.2 on C-acyclic sheaves) belong to a different document, a thesis-style text on ringed sites.
